title: Backend senior scenario cascading outage
question: A downstream service starts responding slowly. Within a few minutes, every service that calls it is also degraded, and the whole platform is effectively down. As the engineer leading incident response, what do you do?
idealAnswer:
Leads with stabilizing the system before root-causing it, e.g. shedding load or failing fast on calls to the slow downstream service (even manually, like scaling it down from the load balancer or feature-flagging off the dependent functionality) to stop the cascade from spreading further

Correctly diagnoses the mechanism: callers are blocking and holding resources (threads, connections) waiting on a slow dependency, so the slowness of one service propagates as resource exhaustion in every caller, not just as slow responses

Talks about clear incident command basics: someone owning the decision-making and communication, status updates going out, avoiding multiple people making uncoordinated changes to the same systems mid-incident

Identifies the durable fix for next time: timeouts and circuit breakers on inter-service calls, so one slow dependency degrades gracefully (fails fast, or serves cached/default data) instead of cascading

Mentions a blameless postmortem afterward focused on why the cascade wasn't contained (missing timeouts/circuit breakers, no load shedding), not just what triggered the initial slowness
